title: Bind Claude telemetry to the durable launcher
description: Prerequisite for task-00e4827dd9374ec79625351d560c82c8. Fresh measurement at HEAD 8557296: launchClaudeWithTelemetry hardwires raw launchClaude and returns only the telemetry handoff, while Foundation dispatch must use createClaudeLauncher(authority) and still needs the exact ClaudeLaunchResult. Add the public runner factory/result surface that executes one authority-bound physical launch and derives the handoff from that same result—never a second launch or a rebuilt observation.
definitionOfDone: A public @moe/runner factory accepts only ClaudeLauncherAuthority, binds createClaudeLauncher(authority), and on invocation calls that launcher exactly once; no caller-supplied deps, launcher function, exit, observation, or telemetry handoff is accepted.

The success arm returns one deeply frozen object containing the exact ClaudeLaunchResult and the ClaudeTelemetryHandoff derived from that same result; REFUSED, EXIT_BEFORE_LAUNCH, ADOPTED and OBSERVED preserve the runner's existing truth, code and layer without restamping.

A malformed/hostile ProviderRunRef refuses at TELEMETRY_INPUT with TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED before authority, store, filesystem, or process effects; generated hostile cases assert a positive case count.

Focused production-surface tests prove one-launch ordering, raw-result identity/binding, blind UNKNOWN behavior, and one accepted same-result control; mutation of the production binding to invoke twice or pair a different result reddens a named assertion.

The new symbol is exported through the public @moe/runner root, the existing daemon manifest and pnpm-lock edge remain valid, and a compiled bare-specifier probe from apps/daemon typechecks and is deleted in the same command.
taskRails: Modify only packages/runner/src/providers/telemetry/claude-telemetry-launch.ts, its focused test, and packages/runner/src/surface/claude-surface.ts; refactor/trim the existing 250-line production source rather than growing it over 250.
Do not expose private launcher defaults, snapshotRunRef, intakeProcessObservation, raw dependencies, or a generic supplied-launcher hook; authority is the existing public ClaudeLauncherAuthority.
Preserve existing ProviderTelemetryCode/layer and Claude launcher refusals exactly; no new wire kind or daemon behavior in this task.
Use TDD, assert exact code/layer and nonzero cases, run runner typecheck/test with nonzero count lines, and name task-00e4827dd9374ec79625351d560c82c8 as the consuming production task.

implementationPlan.description:
THE FOUR ARMS, each asserting the exact truth class, code and layer, and each asserting the raw result travels with the handoff.
- REFUSED: the launcher's own `code` and `layer` appear verbatim as `handoff.launch.reasonCode` / `reasonLayer`; `handoff.telemetryRefusal` carries `TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED` at `TELEMETRY_LAUNCH`; terminal is `REFUSED`, infrastructure `LAUNCH_REFUSED`; and `bound.result.kind === "REFUSED"` is still returned rather than swallowed.
- EXIT_BEFORE_LAUNCH and ADOPTED, as two SEPARATE cases: both take the not-attempted arm with `TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED`, terminal `UNKNOWN`, infrastructure `LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED` — but assert each kind independently, because a single case would stay green if one kind stopped reaching that arm.
- OBSERVED: `truthClass`, digests, timestamps and `exit` all come from `result.observation`, and `infrastructure` is `NONE` only when the exit was observed, the capture parsed AND the launcher proved the run.
- BLIND UNKNOWN BEHAVIOUR: on every non-OBSERVED arm the token, step, model, sequence and receipt facts are UNKNOWN carrying the forwarded code and layer — never zero-filled, never partially summed. Assert the UNKNOWN's code, not merely that the value is not a number.
No restamping: a launcher refusal must never be reported under a TELEMETRY_* code, and a telemetry refusal must never be reported under a launcher code.

One case covering both kinds would stay green the day only one still reached that arm.

BLIND UNKNOWN BEHAVIOUR as a 3-row table with its length asserted first (`toBe(3)`), each row naming the TELEMETRY code its facts must carry: tokens (all four plus coverage UNKNOWN), steps, observedModel, sequence and BOTH receipt digests are `{known:false, code, layer:"TELEMETRY_LAUNCH"}` — the CODE asserted, not merely the absence of a number — plus `JSON.stringify(...)` carrying no `"value"` at all, so a zero-fill or a partial sum reddens here rather than in a consumer. The published factory refuses caller dependencies outright (`composeDurableLauncher` -> DEPENDENCIES_REFUSED), so reaching OBSERVED would require the shipped Windows boundary to spawn a real provider process. It is covered where it IS reachable — on the SAME `handoffOf` derivation both entry points now share — by the pre-existing "binds the launcher's own observation rather than recomputing any of it" (which compares truthClass, all six digests, both timestamps and exit field by field against a control launch's `observation`) and by the INFRASTRUCTURE_CASES sweep, whose NONE row and stderr-failure UNKNOWN row are exactly the earned-NONE rule. The new final case is what makes that transfer legitimate rather than assumed: on the ADOPTED arm, which BOTH entry points can produce, `launchClaudeWithTelemetry`'s handoff and the bound factory's handoff are asserted deep-equal, with a non-vacuity assertion that both really produced ADOPTED. implementationPlan.description:
HOSTILE ProviderRunRef, refused before any effect — DoD item 3.
Generate the hostile cases: null, undefined, a primitive, an array, a Proxy with a throwing `get`, a revoked Proxy, an object with an accessor-backed field, `__proto__`-bearing, missing one required ref field, an empty-string field, a non-NFC field, and a numeric field where a string is required. Assert `cases.length > 0` BEFORE asserting outcomes — a sweep that silently generates zero cases passes while testing nothing.
Every case must return the refusal `{ code: "TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED", layer: "TELEMETRY_INPUT" }` — assert BOTH, never just `ok === false`.
AND ASSERT ZERO EFFECTS, which is the half a return-value assertion cannot see: drive each case through a factory built over a BOOBY-TRAPPED authority whose `consumeGrantDurably` and `commitProcessRegistration` both throw if called, and assert neither was invoked. A hostile ref that reached the launcher would surface as that throw. Pair it with a positive control on the same authority shape — a well-formed ref DOES reach `consumeGrantDurably` — so the zero-effect assertion cannot be passing because the ports are unreachable in this fixture at all.
implementationPlan.note:
HOSTILE RUN REFS, refused before any effect. `npx vitest run packages/runner/src/providers/telemetry/claude-telemetry-launch.test.ts` -> EXIT=0, `Tests 82 passed (82)` (+20). `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck` -> EXIT=0.

POSITIVE CASE COUNT ASSERTED FIRST, in its own case, before any outcome is asserted: `expect(HOSTILE_RUN_REFS.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)`, then `toBe(17)`, then that all 17 labels are DISTINCT (a duplicated label would mean a row silently replaced another).

THE 17 SHAPES: null; undefined; a string primitive; a number primitive; an array; a Proxy with a throwing `get` trap; a revoked Proxy; an accessor-backed `runRef` answering a non-string; a `__proto__`-bearing record whose attemptRef is absent; a record missing `effectIntentId`; an empty `runRef`; a non-ASCII `effectIntentId`; a numeric `attemptRef`; a ref naming another provider; a negative epoch; a fractional epoch; an over-long (201-char) `runRef`.

EVERY case asserts BOTH halves — `code === "TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED"` AND `layer === "TELEMETRY_INPUT"` — never merely `ok === false`.

ZERO EFFECTS, the half a return value cannot see: every case runs through a factory built over a BOOBY-TRAPPED authority whose `consumeGrantDurably` and `commitProcessRegistration` both record and THROW, and asserts the trap log is empty. A hostile ref that reached the launcher would surface as that throw.

POSITIVE CONTROL, on the same authority shape: a WELL-FORMED ref does reach the trap — `fired` equals exactly `["consumeGrantDurably"]` and the launch comes back REFUSED / CLAUDE_LAUNCH_DEPENDENCY_THROWN / GRANT. Without it, the empty trap log would be equally consistent with ports unreachable in this fixture at all, and all 17 rows would prove nothing.

TWO OF THE PLAN'S SUGGESTED SHAPES WERE MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, and are recorded in the suite's own comment rather than asserted into a false claim. `snapshotRunRef` (provider-telemetry-contracts.ts:208) refuses proxies before reading and then reads five fields by name, so: (a) an accessor-backed field is NOT malformed per se — a getter answering a valid string is accepted — so the row is narrowed to "an accessor-backed runRef answering a non-string", which is the shape that genuinely refuses; (b) an own `__proto__` key is ACCEPTED, because the snapshot is total by construction and rebuilds a fresh record from the five read fields, so nothing can be partially adopted. Asserting either as a refusal would have been a fabricated expectation. The `__proto__` shape is instead pinned by a dedicated ACCEPTANCE case: a well-formed `__proto__`-bearing ref is accepted, `handoff.providerRunRef` equals RUN_REF, `Object.hasOwn(..., "__proto__")` is false, the prototype is `Object.prototype`, and the key set is exactly the five contract fields.

The honest observation point is the AUTHORITY — `consumeGrantDurably` is invoked by the real launcher during a real launch — so the one-launch property is asserted by counting authority-port calls, which is a production surface rather than a test seam.
3) CALL `createClaudeLauncher(authority)` PER INVOCATION instead of at factory time. REJECTED: the DoD says the factory BINDS the launcher, and rebinding per call would re-run composition on every launch while making "exactly one launch" harder to reason about. Bound once, closed over.
4) RETURN THE RAW RESULT ONLY ON THE OBSERVED ARM. REJECTED: the consumer needs exit facts precisely on the arms where the handoff is blind. Every arm returns the raw `ClaudeLaunchResult`; only the handoff goes UNKNOWN.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD d2151d49 (the description's 8557296 is stale; every structural claim it makes still holds).

THE FILE IS EXACTLY 250 LINES. `packages/runner/src/providers/telemetry/claude-telemetry-launch.ts` = 250, and task rail 1 forbids growing it past 250 and forbids adding a module. So the factory only fits after extracting the arm-selection body into an internal `handoffOf(providerRunRef, declared, result)` and compressing declarations. That extraction is also what makes the two entry points share ONE derivation instead of two that could disagree.

WHAT `launchClaudeWithTelemetry` DOES TODAY: snapshots the run ref and refuses TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED / TELEMETRY_INPUT BEFORE launching, reads `declared` through the launcher's own `snapshotLaunchSelection`, calls the hardwired `launchClaude(request, options ?? {})`, then branches REFUSED -> blind handoff (TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED / REFUSED / LAUNCH_REFUSED), non-OBSERVED -> blind handoff (TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED / UNKNOWN / LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED), OBSERVED -> parsed handoff. It returns ONLY `{ok, handoff}` — the `ClaudeLaunchResult` is discarded, which is the gap this task closes.

THE AUTHORITY SEAM: `createClaudeLauncher(authority: unknown)` at packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-launcher-authority.ts:204 returns `(value: unknown, options?: ClaudeLaunchOptions) => Promise<ClaudeLaunchResult>`. `ClaudeLauncherAuthority` (claude-launcher-contract.ts:234) has exactly two ports, `consumeGrantDurably` and `commitProcessRegistration`, both returning `unknown` because they cross a process boundary. Typing the new factory's parameter as `ClaudeLauncherAuthority` is the compile-time fence; the launcher still decodes at runtime.

THE FOUR ARMS ARE EXACTLY: `ClaudeLaunchResult = ClaudeLaunchFailure | ClaudeLaunchDuplicate | ClaudeLaunchObserved` (contract:167), where ClaudeLaunchDuplicate.kind is `"ADOPTED" | "EXIT_BEFORE_LAUNCH"` (:149). ADOPTED and EXIT_BEFORE_LAUNCH share the not-attempted arm today, so they need two separate test cases — one case would stay green if a kind stopped reaching it.

ROOT PUBLICATION NEEDS NO INDEX EDIT: packages/runner/src/index.ts:162 is `export * from "./surface/claude-surface.js"`, and claude-surface.ts already re-exports the telemetry module's block (CLAUDE_TELEMETRY_HANDOFF_VERSION, launchClaudeWithTelemetry and six types).
